* **Hello everyone. How are you all? Welcome to my blog.**

---
---
#

Tahaqa is very clever. He realized that Bayek is no ordinary warrior. His fighting skills are extraordinary. So he wanted to take advantage of the opportunity. He told Bayek that if he helped him against the bandits, he would give him some important secret information about the Scarab.

Bayek did not want to miss the opportunity to get new information about the Scarab. So he agreed to help Tahaqa.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU3DnB5Rw2ef4QWyj8FsSQkqHEj8hgaJEzDSMFy7z62eP/snapshot_23.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTEGMJy9ceaLbgKvaFzjGtNcfmfv5cqaf8Dhrg1KWTk6b/snapshot_24.png)

When Tahaqa and Bayek came out, they saw that several of their companions were standing ready. They would all launch an operation against the bandits together.

Tahaqa said that the bandits had taken refuge in a cave a few kilometers away from here. They would go there and ambush them. Then they all set off for the cave.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfKUuTYQYfzwPLLXfCcRnubFEZidKiVVrhL42NfsqeBWB/snapshot_25.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme5cK89PhAvdqNx79BSGBcKNehzqn3EFhxS9d6amxn9XH/snapshot_26.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW1XW6WQgrHeL57XbFLts24UgxueQ6Xr2s9a8795DyZLY/snapshot_27.png)

They reached the cave. The cave was on the bank of a small river. Although the place looked peaceful, it was a hideout for dangerous bandits. When they reached there, everyone decided to attack directly. Everyone was very angry at that time. They did not wait a moment. They entered the cave directly and started the attack.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfJJPY6EkSUfxTVKTAFBuxwc2XZEKN3cGEd2c6zxHzcHh/snapshot_28.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXqk3s2QTtWrUfddnKsw6WdhRTQvzKs7fqW9qZbPkDjSy/snapshot_29.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVFc2LVYdCV1Xa2L8kiBMVwwHYUwVw14YQcuP7tytpbJN/snapshot_30.png)

However, the bandits were not as strong as before. In the previous major battle in the city of Letopolis, most of the bandit group had died. Those who survived were injured and frightened. They were fighting with swords nearby, and Bayek was standing, observing the situation. After watching the battle for a while, he took out his bow.

Then he started shooting arrows one after another, finishing off the bandits in a matter of seconds. Tahaqa was amazed by Bayek's extraordinary archery. He began to praise Bayek.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSJCFPXUj9uwKyeXwLV7zNoKz8VoECyUvW6eXF1UGS2xk/snapshot_31.png)

When the battle was about to end, the leader of the bandit group tried to escape from the cave. Tahaqa quickly ran and caught him. Then he started fighting with the leader. Bayek did not interfere there. Because he understood that Tahaqa had a personal anger against this man. So, he had the right to kill him.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSVpDZWKsxsCDiTNSX1rhy1RQFFuqDdguM3DMoPRGB7QN/snapshot_32.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYrc67D3HXUVMonopDDzm9uA5Frv4tVTW2MXE1jB4ku3B/snapshot_33.png)

After killing the leader, Tahaqa and Bayek go back into the cave. There, they find Tahaqa's eldest son imprisoned in a cage. They open the cage and rescue him.

Tahaqa then hugged Bayek and thanked him. He said that if it weren't for Bayek, he might never have gotten his son back. He invited Bayek to his house. Everyone will eat and have fun together.

---
#
So far, the whole incident has been quite enjoyable.

On the one hand, as Bayek helped Tahaqa, on the other hand, there was an opportunity to get new information about the Scarab.

* **Now the question is :**

> **1. Does Tahaqa really know important information about the Scarab?**

> **2. And how much will that information help Bayek?**

All the answers are hidden in the next mission.

---

* **See you all in the next mission. Goodbye.**

---

---

links.title: A Day in My Life Blog: A Job Well Done for My Nephew Baby King2x on thier Summer Class at School Today. He can Now Read and Write. Thank God! 👏🙏😇
links.body: **Have a Blessed Day to all ASEAN Hivers and all my Fellow Hivers all over the World!** The Summer Class of my Nephew Baby King2x was just started and he has been doing well together with his classmates. We thank God for the life of their Teacher who patiently teach her new Students. The schedule of the Summer Class will only last for two weeks, and it was just started last week and will continue this week. I can still see that my Nephew is excited going to School. For my blog post today, this is what I am about to share, the happenings during the new day of their Summer Class. As what I always do, I will never forget to give thanks most especially to my supporters. To the Admins and all Curators, I will always thank all of you for always supporting me. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXpSmtEhvKR5RaqpWMKBg3tZ2kkokvrCWpXPTWyd7oUiS/1779106025100.png) We all know that at this age of 5 or 6 years old, we needed to monitor and help them most especially in their studies that is why, we're very happy to know that their is a Summer Class here in the School as this allows the students to remember and recap what they have studied on their Kindergarten classes. To support my Nephew, even though both of his parents are not around as they both working abroad I am always here to support and help him in his studies, as will as to his Summer Class now. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdYNwDnyeNuAhXrXQw2csQRmmbUy8eSX86mxVqQRrWbMF/1779106675907.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTGqRdg5xf8MQicrKGVhkXKkoYVzRWpmibBV7CkQpv3Y3/1779106675991.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPTE3vdtyJegJQvcYjB32mtHcewDs4vjTNdp6dVQVHZRj/1779106676068.jpg) Last week, the Teacher given all of her students a homework and it is a reading tasks. And when we were at home, I always make sure that my Nephew will do whatever tasks or homework given to him by his Teacher. Now, in today's class we went to the School on time and it just a time also when the Teacher started the class. Just after the opening prayer, my Nephew went to his teacher bringing the paper with the homework and told his Teacher that he did his homework at home. That is why, the Teacher told him to read in the front what he has read at home. Even though my Nephew is a bit shy, he still go in front and read. He only read the title, and it is still very good for him for a job well done. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmf9duraisZDWpmE2KPmkQ7yiqRaAvMozidnSRhMz1cGzM/1779107091890.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbHjhd2D2mThXLgmfnMDwgkTGLB1rN8K9NmXiwBSirySr/1779107091965.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmck7jwbGeEdCKVMfotNwAfbsMJgfgJuuKLgVwgkLywaZS/1779107092012.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb38uNdQgPBP9XQGG5tiGc1ptn4SQQA4xc5z4MW8gcEfr/1779107092061.jpg) After my Nephew read the homework, they have now begins the next tasks which is again a reading tasks. The Teacher uses a YouTube Video which is a good material for this generation. The teacher starts now teaching to them some unfamiliar words in which they didn't learned from their Kindergarten class. And even though it is new for all of them, the students still participated and do their best as they can. I just thank God for my Nephew can already read those unfamiliar words for them as compared to some of his classmates who is struggling to read it. He is indeed doing good during their class. To make the class more exciting, the Teacher decided to have challenged for all of them. A two students will be tasks to read the short sentence and whoever read it first correctly will step one forward until they won the game. At first match, my Nephew didn't win as he didn't read the short sentence first, but in the second match, finally he got read first the sentence that is why he won the second match which make him very happy after. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPrUiekqkXU9EWFx3c9Z75soUsYuPrA1ok3YTdBtgrAEk/1779107674603.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXUADuMTJ67vXKG1o3RiHxWJUvJnjkFVucyMw8FHdo9na/1779107674690.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPkNwD81eVeo9hJwqoCRtQaymYGgC8VuRBmzwMsvg1Zom/1779107674745.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdj8VxP4g33nCmLZmBnrkFyhYX1a2psnZQSyDUqnyEAJt/1779107674791.jpg) All of the Students has been doing well while reading those short sentence, and thank God for the Teacher who also do her best she can just for her students will learn during this Summer Class. The next tasks which is the last one before we go back home is a writing activity. The Teacher shown some words that the students should have to familiar and needed to write it in their notebook. They needed to write all of this words in their notebook in order for them to go home. That is why, my Nephew immediately get his notebook and pencil, and went near to what they needed to write. He and his classmates are now busy and focus on the writing activity given to them, in order for them to go home. I can see that my nephew is struggling in writing but I let him write it by his own so he can learn more. I am very happy and proud of him because even without my help, he even did his writing activity and when I looked at his notebook, it is still didn't write well but it is much better than before, and that, my Nephew has been doing great today. After all the writing activity has done, it is now time for us to go home and all glory and honor belongs to God alone. This would be all for today's post, and until next time again, I just want to thank everyone in advance who will drop by on my blog post. **To God be all the Glory!** 😇🙌☝️ **Your Friend** **_@godlovermel25_**

Greetings hivers.

Finishing the editing of the photos from this birthday session with a young woman who decided that 29 was the perfect age to immortalize her image.

body.title: Jervis Bay rock pool, family and orchid day : May 17 2026
body.body:
A different day lining up. First stop drive down to Huskisson Beach to meet up with my son and his family. Parked up and walking across the park to where we last met. Hear footsteps behind. Apparently the minute Scarlett saw me shie took off to run after me. We jumped steps a bit and then went for a walk ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/35b73c0d-0704-485a-bf2f-1f240b8ddf09.jpg) Admired flowers along the way - banksia ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/fd77c576-4865-431b-bf47-fc392a0eb804.jpg) Lifted her up at one of the beach lookouts. Can we walk the beach? We did. Photo from way back - mum and the two girls at water's edge ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/ea0f362d-2eda-467f-b552-f3ac1a16fce0.jpg) A bit of a geology lesson. The black rock is Wandrawandian siltstone going back 250 million years. The notable part is the remnants of other rocks embedded when sea levels rose 120 metres ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/7d0db8d2-7ff3-4020-beba-e962e8027247.jpg) A piece of quartz ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/55b4b913-1235-435d-ab3f-bf851f3da506.jpg) Shells too - two types in shot. Amazing how well preserved they are ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/c5b319df-f7c9-45d7-ba6d-1876c4a19dec.jpg) We studied snails - they eat the algae - just like the fish tank at home ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/d435d5ee-4c2b-4e4d-b7b0-c6e5951d4ce0.jpg) Rock Pool study - Scarlett, Daddy and Daddyman studying snails eating algae ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/d7c71407-d8af-4e79-838f-ee75b511384c.jpg) Clouds broke a bit to show the blue water of Jervis Bay. Was a great catch up. Daddyman took off to walk a track not walked ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/23f0b567-46d0-4c5b-8839-8a52f95f70f2.jpg) Had to walk a different trail as there was a hazard reduction burn on one I wanted to walk - walked a new track ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/11b5da51-3dda-444e-9a8d-512e36ba623f.jpg) Bonnet orchid leaves ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/7a7cf093-4af3-49c7-bf02-1a5a2bfc4d3b.jpg) Slender rice flower ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/5614e9ff-3ec3-43f7-8c0c-a3da1fc74536.jpg) NSW coral heath flower - epacris pulchella ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/9052e468-39a5-42db-8e27-7ae263d40c1b.jpg) A small clearing offered up parson's bands orchid - a lot in flower ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/ff0623e4-cdf4-4d6b-9d06-8f9752c4c6ca.jpg) Key to ID is the large leaf forming after flowering and hairy spike - eriochilus cucullatus ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/4e5143bb-479a-4728-bfab-02a33f66dd3d.jpg) Double header ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/b74ab42d-04e8-4300-abca-a47da068cf69.jpg) Mushroom action ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/546367c3-fc46-4d49-bfe1-1f6adb54648f.jpg) Funky light effect on this double header ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/9e5be248-e765-475a-87f0-5f76e47f97ff.jpg) Banskia - good to see so many open. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/3011cd0a-7d85-4d22-ad06-dd5b5a8d13bc.jpg) A seeded orchid - not seen these before - the droop of the pedicel has me wondering on ID ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/c821bbe0-d13c-414b-af2f-5b3d9b34d5ac.jpg) Matching rosette is a cluster of leaves more than most greenhoods. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/45463630-5b1d-4d1e-a006-0e1dfba1cd89.jpg) Hibbertia ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/d226de8c-b185-415f-9296-d358f1acbb4c.jpg) Snake orchid - cymbidium suave - seed pd showing. For some reason they prosper on these low cut tree trunks ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/3a74487c-84c9-4933-a60b-492bb85e5071.jpg) Wondering how they get there. Seeds from plants higher up. Bird poo? ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/65e512b8-5844-44a9-8f31-9558dab7349f.jpg) Found a fee more parson's bands orchids. body.title: Hot tempered people can be very destructive.
body.body:
We are all welcome back to this beautiful edition of hive learners community week 218, episode 1. It gladens my heart when see us talking about topics that can bring about change in the society.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmawwbvnPhcatvNKYw9KtDsGUS6Tjh9LwKo5yyVobapiH5/1779108181586.jpg)

For me this amazing community is lia school, because every week and also three times we come to discuss different topics. Everyone s allowed to bring us a discussion from any angle and that has really helped us to learn new things capable of changing our lives. Who knows what would have become of me, if I had not met this community? I say this because of the value that this special community has added to my entire life. Alot are testifying about it, but they don't know where I got it from. Kudos to all the moderators of #hive learners community. You have done a lot for us the members. We just keep growing everyday with each topic.

Moving forward I really want yo say that people who are hot temper are very destructive. In fact you won't know about their destructive nature until you come closer to them. Let me tell us a story and this is a true life story.

When was 18 years old I was privileged to live with one of my aunt who as at that time was still a single lady. Men kept coming to ask her to marry them, but she was a bit skeptical about getting married because of what she had seen in other marriages. There is this particular guy she loves so much and he was also serious about getting married to her. We were all happy for her, but al of a sudden she started withdrawal from him and when we asked her she said that she don't think she can cope with his hot temper. She said that when ever this guy is angry he can just pick anything close to him and throw to anyone close by. he have witnessed this time without number and she said that the best thing for her is to stay away from him so that he can get another girl that he will marry. The guy refused to give up on her, he made all the promises in this world saying that he will change, but she refused him because of how dangerous his temper is. She said that with what she has seen, this man will kill her one dain the name of hot temper. The marriage plans just desolved and tey went there separate ways. 


MY CANDIDATE ADVISE 
I think and also believe that anyone with such should get help from anger management therapist. I know that there are some people who are trained to help them out of it. No one should manage such situation.  When you stay close to them you will understand that it is dangerous. They are destructive and can kill at any slightest mistake. They only fell sorry after they might have done what is in their mind. Just talking to them won't solve the problem, but they should get help. At the process of getting help, I strongly believe that prayers i very much needed. I believe in God and I what God can not do, can not exist.

body.title: Palm Oil Unloading Process at Tepin Lada PKS Today.
body.body:
Today I returned to my normal activities as a driver transporting fresh fruit bunches (FFB). This morning the weather was overcast, and the roads in the mill area were quite muddy after the rain. Despite this, operations at the factory continued as usual.


***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNaLKS6GdTbKwN7Ho3qAr5FFcYVnyubGAyKUkTv4gkjFU/1779107806900.jpg)


Upon arriving at the PKS, I immediately parked my car in the unloading area. I saw a large pile of palm fruit awaiting further processing. Workers were also busy arranging the fruit to ensure a swift and orderly unloading process.

***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmay4R59w8QnYKQZEeAK54ToDq9DDfzfUKLCWVoVkm1hcF/1779107858735.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWAfaQmtVgnW7LkEGed39HPky5s8s7U4Bj69M7WhXRt6H/1779107912272.jpg)


The yellow truck I was driving today was carrying a load of palm oil from a smallholder plantation. The journey to the factory was quite challenging due to the slippery and potholed roads. But it all felt worth it when we finally arrived safely and the unloading process went smoothly.

***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWEhahHoeUvBMiLrhBWrXw2kuey928MvhjXTVVTvqkpQW/1779107947934.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNgiihmj9EAie5snfmRQ6tvWwEN5E3Mw9S4sjoEiqN578/1779107995922.jpg)

Working in the palm oil industry is indeed full of challenges. Sometimes you have to face rain, heat, damaged roads, and even long lines at the palm oil mill. But many families depend on this work for their livelihood. That's why I remain enthusiastic about my work every day.
I also enjoy sharing my daily activities with my friends at Hive. I hope this simple post provides a glimpse into the working environment at the palm oil mill.

That concludes our brief life story. I hope my hive/ecency friends can forgive any imperfections, both in writing and word choice.

Best regards, @Djisamsoe

body.title: TELEPATHY
body.body:
Hello everyone you're welcome to my blog today


Telepathy when you hear telepathy what comes to mind is communication through thoughts I mean I have never seen that happen but only in movies. More like movie tricks and all this magic that happens behind the scene.


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmbrP9KPPaSxdxqZH5LuQoU9zj4ZXPCdfaoTTKEGnEdJZJ/13358.png 




 To be honest sometimes I would love to communicate through my thoughts where nobody would hear a thing about what I want to say to the next person I would really love that but is it worth it.

Have we ever thought of it this way , is it everything that we can share through our thoughts or are there some things that we really want to say out loud. Communication through our thoughts is very vital if I have a partner and I want to tell him some lovely things about him or encouraging him in my own little way at that point I wish they could read my mind and know what am thinking about and I'll be happy to just sit them without saying a word and let in this silence do it's magic.

Communicating telepathically has a very huge advantage nobody will be able to hear your thoughts if you don't want them to know, your secrets are safe with you because you don't have to say them out loud you can only share your thoughts with someone that you trust so much. Because these days walls have ears and we all mind what we see to avoid our secrets getting out to the wrong hands.

What are the disadvantages of communicating telepathically well our thoughts could be easily misunderstood. There are somethings that you have to open your mouth explain you can't explain them by just thinking about them so you don't get misunderstood by the other person.


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYtFLV18cgdfJnFW1LpwCGAej4YBaeAJpSLNkm8npFLva/2659.png 



Communicating telepathically means that we will not open our mouth to talk but only to eat . we might end up forgetting how to talk or how to use words and alphabets. So in as much as communicating telepathically would be really nice , I leave that to my imaginations.

Thank you for stopping by my blog today

So if $Hive happens to hit $1, I will feel on top of the world. Full Metal Ox Day 1905
Monday 18, May 2026

![1970.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW9oTLQFxL8KAzGpvwzJ9Vxz6rJgmJppxBjHPEBkBgKKm/1970.png)

Today's Episode:   https://odysee.com/@Noxsoma:2/1905_full_5-18-26_1970_promos:1?r=47k2ScJsm9Uex9eETqgCCA8q1fukdST9 
Channels: go to noxsoma.substack.com and subscribe.

Chapter 3. Antediluvian Demographics.

Perhaps in a decade or two, researchers will get to the Sumerian cuneiform tablets that will provide a census of the antediluvian world. Any species as anal as the Annunaki, Enili in particular, would want to keep track of their assets. Just as a time stamp, let’s say it’s the 200,000th Earth Year that the Annunaki have been operation on the planet that they call, Ki.” They have successfully created a slave species, (and are in denial about it). This species can procreate on its own. So no more lab grown miners. The lil apes are probably poppin’ em out on site.  

So let’s take our own census. 

There would be a population of Annunaki that were born on Nibiru. 
There would be a population of Annunaki that were born on Earth, and have never been to Nibiru. 
Class-wise, there would be direct descendants of Anu. Both, Enlil & Enki were his sons and had spouses. If I am not mistaken, Enki’s wife carried some hybrid seeds, as did Ninmah, and at least seven other, probably more, Annunaki females. What happened to those hybrid kids? Did they become breeders? 

The labor caste, the Igigi, were probably not only in the mines. But also on Earth and the weigh station on Mars. The mines, by the way, were in Southern Africa. So as hybrids, I suppose we can call them “humans” now,  born of hybrid females, they were sent to the mines. In one researcher’s fantasy film, the narrator says the “primitive workers”, (I think they were called “lulus) labored in the mines without complaint. I suppose not. If you were born to toil and you know nothing else, then what is there to complain about? That was the whole point was it not?  

Okay, let’s set this up to be the least complicated as possible. 

Immigrants, or we could call them, “invaders.” Nibiru-born Annunaki. 
Earthers, Annunaki, including Igigi born on Earth. 
Hybrid females. Half Annunaki, half hominid. Certainly breeders. Possibly domestics, if not test subjects. 
Hybrid males, (miners). Maybe studs. Laborers. Maybe a few were sent to the mines early on. But their Annunaki moms, might have objected and kept their sons, especially the first born, close. 

There were certainly sexual liaisons between invaders and human women, as well as Earthers and hybrids. This is on the record. Once again, right back to original sin. 

In a hundred years, let alone the 3600 earth years that is a single orbit of Nibiru around Helios, there would be quite the diverse population in the fertile crescent. The Australopithecus africanus genes would have been all but eliminated. 
There may or may not have been any breeding going on in Southern Africa. If I had to guess, because most of this is guess work anyway, I’d say that there was. The aliens would send the hybrids which were genetically closer to Africanus, to the gold mines, with Igigi over seers, of course, and a community of “humans” probably emerged. One of those, “mining towns.” 

The fiction that emerged out of the Sumerian tablets, has primarily, (I’d even say, “only”), to do with the region of the Sinai Peninsula. After the slave species is successfully created, they are forgotten about. It’s a very typical supremacist mentality. Whether one is referring to the Space Alien elites, or those who translated the tablets. 

One of the first questions I had, rhetorical of course, is, “what happened to the primal species from which the hybrids were made?” Recall, we are using Australopithecus africanus as a “place holder.” We don’t know whether they were the invaders’ victims or not. Quite likely there were many types of bipedal hominids used.  But some species fit the bill. (If we are to believe this chronicle.) So what happened to said species, and why? Certainly it’s extinct by now, but how?  

It’s very convenient to blame everything on the deluge. We will get to that. Are you still with us? 

In the main Mesopotamian cities, Eridu, Nippur, and Babylon, it is our contention that the majority of the population, of so-called “humans” were mostly of Annunaki bloodlines, including Igigi. There are a few exceptions, more examples of “original sin,” that makes for a good flood myth. But Mind finds it very unlikely that after the first 100 years, and certainly the first millenium, that there would be much of the Africanus strain left in the population. 

If you happen to know better, or even different. Holler. 


Here’s what Genesis, Chapter 6 has to say about the population.  

“When human beings began to increase in number on the earth and daughters were born to them, the sons of God, (aka Annunaki earth-born, or otherwise), saw that the daughters of humans were beautiful,  (no more hominid traits), and they married any of them they chose.” Then the Lord, (Enlil) said, “My Spirit will not contend with humans forever, for they are mortal; their days will be a hundred and twenty years.” 
What was Enlil’s problem with “human beings?” The Annunaki chronicles says it’s the “noise.” The noise that humans made was hindering his sleep? Okay. Where was he sleeping?  But I doubt that this is the only complaint, or the ony reason he wanted to wipe them out. It’s probably a matter of ratio. Or maybe they were just a bunch of freeloaders rocking and rolling all night long and partying every day.  Enlil as “Lord of Command” could see the writing on the wall.  
The humans were getting out of control and soon they would be completely unmanageable and would become a threat to the establishment.    
Back to Genesis.  
“The Nephilim, (could be the Igigi, so-called lesser gods), were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, (after the flood, presumably), when the sons of God, (literally Enki’s lineage and Enki himself), went to the daughters of humans and had children by them. They were the heroes of old, men of renown.” (This could very possibly be interpreted as these, “heroes” becoming a threat to the gods. The warning against eating of the fruit of knowledge, for “they will become like us.”)   
“The Lord saw how great the wickedness of the human race had become on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all the time. The Lord regretted that he had made human beings on the earth, and his heart was deeply troubled. So the Lord said, “I will wipe from the face of the earth the human race I have created, and with them the animals, the birds and the creatures that move along the ground, for I regret that I have made them.” But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.” 


First of all, twice in these verses, 1 thru 8, the “Lord” takes credit for having, “made” and “created”   
the human race. 

Here’s some context, because on one side of the table we have the Sumerian tablets, and on the other side Genesis Chapter 6. Let’s start with Gen 6. “The Lord is complaining about humans.” In the tablets it’s Enlil who did all of the complaining about the “noise pollution.” Enlil was against the creation of humans from the start. So Gen 6 is combining the two Space Alien brothers into a single “speaker.” 

In the tablets, Enki is the creator of humans, and continuously circumvents Enlil’s commands in an effort to preserve humanity. Which he created.   

Your boy still cannot shake the idea that these antediluvian “humans” are a thousand plus generations away from the original “primitive worker” model, who have been completely forgotten and play no role in Old Testament scripture. (Maybe they are already extinct.)  

Let’s reduce this to “archetypes.” The Lord represents the alien elite. Humans represent the hoi polloi, the rabble, the great unwashed masses that multiply too quickly and make too much noise. Noah represents purity among the race of humans. Like a long lost Rockefeller kid, whose mom was close enough to “our crowd” to be worth saving.   

It should be noted that there are at least two characters who played the lead role in, “The Flood,” before Noah got the part. You should check them out if you haven’t already. 

The flood didn’t happen all at once. And it wasn’t a surprise to the Annunaki Elites. They knew it was coming, many as many as ten shars, (that’s one complete orbit of Nibiru around Helios, our common sun.) That’s 36,000 Earth orbits. 

Another mind-blower, before we wrap up this chapter. These aliens never die! Enlil, Enki and Ninmah were there from the beginning. Oh yeah, this is fiction. Almost forgot. Nonetheless, Mind is attempting to calculate a population that increases in its increasing and multiplies in its multitudes, for 100,000 earth years. There’s little if any talk about people dying until the cataclysm. Maybe Cain killed Abel before the flood. I don’t quite recall. That’s another thing. Without a white board or vibe-coding apps, We get a bit confused. And if I watch one more Annunaki video, I might just defenestrate myself. However, in Gen 6 when The Lord decides that it’s 120 and out for humans, the implication is, to your humble vagabond, that there was no expiration date. And then how was he going to pull that off anyway?  

The Cosmogony behind Vagabond Philosophy, is that humans were created by aliens to be a slave species, but, the population became a threat, and to this day, human critters are marked for death. And other pleasant thoughts.  

Next chapter. No God or Alien caused the great flood. But they knew it was coming like FDR knew Pearl Harbor would be attacked.  


See you then.

Нормально оплачувана робота за кордоном, звісно ж, є. Але більшість проблем із працевлаштуванням в українців виникають через посередників, «сірі» схеми і завищені очікування.
Розкладемо по сегментах. 

📦 Склади / логістика
Де платять:
Німеччина, Нідерланди, Чехія, Польща
Великі склади (Amazon, DHL, Zalando), офіційні контракти через агентства.
Реальність:
8–14 €/год (залежить від країни)
Стабільні зміни, але фізично важко. Часто - житло від роботодавця, але не безкоштовне.
Де обман:
Обіцяють 15–18 €/год без мови і досвіду,
за \

житло потім віднімають із зарплати, підписуєш один контракт - працюєш на іншого роботодавця.

🏗 Будівництво
Де платять:
Німеччина, Бельгія, Франція - якщо є досвід (муляр, електрик, плиточник).
Реальність:
12–25 €/год
Готівка або частково офіційно, гарні зарплати - лише у фахівців.
Де обман:
«25 €/год усім» - брехня, затримки виплат або «зник роботодавець».
Робота без контракту = ризик не отримати нічого.

Далі буде.

Bueno, ahí estaba, a todo volumen, el hit de he mencionado.

\\*\n\n

>Vi sonrisas de todas estas mujeres. Creo que todas entendimos, sin emitir palabra alguna, sin conocernos. La situación en la que estábamos todas, estoy convencida eran diversas. body.title: Regional Champs
body.body:
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTxPx3SZTrWk8Y7LX4h6XiuJomBNwEcLidKkfHgGNEpuq/PXL_20250620_134716805.webp)

----------------------------

Well, I'm clearly not talking about the Detroit Pistons with that title.  They dropped game 7 last night to find themselves out of the NBA playoffs.  Honestly, they should have and could have buttoned things up well before last night, but that is a whole different subject.  Instead, today I am going to talk about the NCAA Division I softball tournament and the results of the regional round. 

I'm not going to dig into each quad, because that would be quite tedious. Just know that a lot of softball took place this past weekend and many teams found themselves fighting for their lives to make it to the Super Regional games.  Remember, we started with something like 64 teams at the beginning of the tournament and that has now been cut down to 16 teams via double elimination play in the regional games.  

The super regional games will be a best of three format that will cut the field in half down to eight teams.  Those eight teams will then play double elimination again to determine the two teams facing off in the championship series. 

In the Tuscaloosa quad, number 1 seed Alabama came out on top besting SE LA, Belmont, and USC Upstate.  In Baton Rouge, number 4 seed LSU survived their quad against South Alabama, Akron, and 5 seed Virginia Tech to secure their super regional game against Alabama.   That should be an exciting series!

In Tallahassee, number 3 seed Florida State was eliminated along with Jax State, and Stetson for number 6 seed UCF to punch their ticket to the super regionals.  They will be facing 2 seed UCLA after the Bruins took down 7 seed South Carolina, CALBAP, and CSFULL.

In Fayetteville, number 2 seed Arkansas slipped into the super regional after beating out  7 seed Washington, Fordham, and South Florida.  That sets them up against 3 seed Duke who sent 6 seed Arizona, Howard, and Marshall on the bus back home.

Rounding out the left side of the bracket in Stillwater, we had 1 seed Nebraska dominating their quad taking out 8 seed Louisville, South Dakota, and Grand Canyon.  The Cornhuskers will be facing a 4 seed Oklahoma State team that also ran their quad with zero losses against 5 seed Stanford, Eastern Illinois, and Princeton

Before I jump to the other side of the bracket, I should point out that UCF and Duke are the only two teams who really faced any kind of adversity to make it to the super regional.  Duke actually had to fight their way through the second half of the losers bracket to beat Arizona after dropping their second game to them 10 to 1.  They then hammered Marshal 11 to 1, and beat Arizona twice in a row to win their spot in the Super Regional.

On the other hand, UCF just had a quick loss in the first game of the finals to force a second game.

In the Norman quad we have 1 seed Oklahoma taking out 8 seed Kansas, Michigan, and Binghamton to secure their spot against 5 seed Mississippi State in Euguene.  Miss State took down 4 seed Oregon, Idaho State, and St. Mary to make it to the super regional.

In Lubock 3 seed Texas Tech advances after downing 6 seed Ole Miss, Marist, and Boston U.  Which sets them up to face 2 seed Florida from the Gainesville quad.  The gators topped 7 seed Texas State, Florida A&M, and Georgia Tech.

In Knoxville, 2 seed Tennessee is going to be facing 3 seed Georgia from the Athens quad.  The Volunteers took down 7 seed Virginia, Northern Kentucky, and Indiana while Georgia beat out 6 seed Clemson, C of C, and UNC G to secure their spot.

Finally, 5 seed Arizona State won out over 4 seed Texas A&M, McNeese, and UConn to punch their ticket n the College Station quad against the Austin quad which saw 1 seed Texas taking out 8 seed Wisconsin, Wagner, and Baylor.

I should point out that none of the teams in this side of the bracket had to fight out of the losers bracket to get to the super regionals.  It was a straight shot for all of them.  

I should also point out, UCLA and Nebraska are the only two teams from the Big Ten left in the tournament.  I'm pulling for Nebraska personally.

body.title: Water Is Nowhere To Be Found, So We Bought Two Water Tanks To Solve The Problem/ El Agua Brilla Por Su Ausencia, Compramos Dos Tanques De Agua Para Solucionar [ENG-ESP]
body.body:
>

Hello, everyone.

Hey everyone, I hope you're all doing well. Well, as you can see from the title, it's another adventure I've had here in the country. Stick around and I'll tell you all about it. Water remains that critical problem—a service so necessary, as are all of them, but I think this one is even more so, since we use it to bathe, drink, wash dishes, and more. It’s become an exhausting routine to get up at dawn just to fill buckets or tanks. On my sister’s last trip, she left disappointed, saying that people suffer a lot because of this issue, and she told us to look into buying two more cylindrical tanks, each with a capacity of 1,000 liters. We shopped around for prices and found a hardware store that sold them for $180 each—it was the cheapest place, so to speak; elsewhere, a single tank cost between $200 and $300. We paid for delivery, which brought them right to the front of the house. Before buying them, we had to measure the doorway, since it’s a mistake to buy them without knowing if they’ll fit—this already happened to a neighbor. It’s very important to keep this in mind; sometimes, when we’re in a hurry, we overlook that detail. Because of the two main doors, we planned to bring it into the house through the backyard if it didn’t fit, since it would then go to a small storage room we have there. We bought it with the pressure control included—which is what helps turn the pump off automatically when the water runs out—and its floats to mark the water level. We did all that work to alleviate the water crisis a little bit, which isn’t easy at all, but at least with this, we won’t run out of water as early. I hope you enjoyed my story. Thank you all Note: These photos were taken from my phone and edited In: Canva

>Separators
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/eve66/23tGwQ9PTdcLGhdgdVToYFZeRnY1T3ux5FhspwX5hhXgM2TeSzAz4RQzmDPSHuziMPTmv.png

Hola A Todos.

Hola mi gente espero que se encuentren bien bueno como verán el titulo una aventura más resolviendo aquí en el país quédate y te cuento.
El agua sigue siendo ese problema critico un servicio tan necesario todos lo son pero pienso que este mucho más ya que con él nos bañamos consumimos, lavamos los platos y más, se volvió una rutina agotante pararse de madrugada para lograr llenar tobos o tanques, en el último viaje de mi hermana ella se fue decepcionada ya que dice que se sufre mucho con este tema, y pues nos dijo que averiguáramos para comprar 2 tanques más cilíndricos de capacidad de mil litros cada uno, estuvimos buscando precios y dimos con una ferretería que tenía cada uno en 180$ fue el lugar más barato por así decirlo en otros lugares un solo tanque costaba desde 200$ a 300$, pagamos el delivery que lo trajo hasta el frente de la casa.
Antes de comprarlos se tuvo que medir la puerta ya que es un error comprar sin saber si pasara, ya le ocurrió a una vecina esto es muy importante tenerlo en cuenta a veces por estar apurados omitimos ese detalle, por las dos puertas principales es que teníamos pensado pasarlo a la casa por el patio si no pasaba, ya que luego iría a un pequeño deposito que tenemos allí, se compró con su bomba incluida el pres control que es el que ayuda a apagar la bomba automáticamente cuando el agua ya se va, sus flotadores para marcar el nivel de agua, se fue haciendo todo ese trabajo para mejorar un poco la crisis que existe de agua que no está nada fácil, pero al menos con esto no nos pararemos tan temprano, espero les haya gustado mi relato.

body.title: Anger Is Natural; Destruction Is A Choice.
body.body:
> 


## Hello, everyone.
I welcome you to my blog and another wonderful edition of the Hive Learners' featured post. Anger is a natural thing for humans; we all get angry once in a while, but how we act and react when angry matters a lot because after anger there is still life to live. Many people have made decisions they regret to this date out of anger; some took certain actions out of anger, and to this date they are paying the price of those actions, and that only leaves them with regret. Over the years I have come to realize that 99% of actions and decisions made out of anger are ones we end up regretting when we calm down. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNxGgivLJD6BoicpgyTWizKbroQJxyovqgiBMoLtyS7dd/1779107386401.jpg)

[Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/man-in-black-crew-neck-t-shirt-smiling-BxHnbYyNfTg)

Anger is one of the things that stand in the way of our progress; many people have missed out on opportunities that could have pushed them to the next level all because they claim to be quick-tempered and get angry easily. Some under the umbrella of claiming to be hot-tempered or quick-tempered even destroy things. I once had a neighbor who, whenever his girlfriend gets angry, first of all looks for something to break; if it is not plates, then it is his electronics or gadgets. Sometimes she even carries a knife and chases him around the compound all because she is hot-tempered, and that did not make any sense to me. 

Whether hot-tempered or not, we are all humans, and we all get angry, so why doesn't the boyfriend get angry and do the same? Why does it have to be you who destroys things and hides under the umbrella of \

? We all get angry, and the difference between us is that you being hot-tempered means you get angry faster and over little things, while those that are not hot-tempered take time before they are triggered, but then anger is anger whether it happens rapidly or slowly, but it is funny how it is only you that tears the house and apartment apart.\n\nAfter their fights you hear them apologize and say, \

That is a big lie; that is her trying to avoid responsibility and accountability. Anyone who, after their actions, tries to make excuses is just trying to avoid accountability and responsibility, and that proves that she knows exactly what she is doing. I don't think anyone should tolerate a human being that has chosen to behave like an animal. I am still trying to understand the level of anger that will cause me to look at a television hanging on the wall, and then I pull it out and hit it on the ground, knowing fully well how much it cost. 

<center>
<div class=\

> How Do We As A Society Handle This Issue? ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRJA4wN95kPtKe3okXTzZZ5WLW1pZhxKZE86N97gr2HkY/1779107386310.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/woman-with-black-hair-smiling-9nrc57bkWYM) We as a society must punish those with tempers like this; after destruction and when calm, they should be asked to buy back everything that was destroyed in the cause of their anger. I think after they replace a destroyed item once or twice they will learn to control their emotions. We as a society should also try to teach emotional control a lot earlier, like in schools and in family homes, and kids who have tendencies like this should be given attention to and made to understand that it is not a good path to follow or stay on. I believe if the issue is detected early and given the attention it needs, the world will be free of people with that type of anger.

body.title: I became a grandmother even as a single lady because my cats decided to create a family
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXZP5DxdHUKCjjnbbhUAoA4w28cD5ouPjPVwK5Yg9jAdu/img_5735.jpg)
When I lost my second cat, *Gingerbread*, I thought my heart would never recover. The goodbye hurt so much that I promised myself I would never get another cat again. I told myself that Tofi, my fluffy Persian boy, was enough. No more attachments and no more heartbreaks.

But life has a funny way of breaking promises, even one made to yourself.

One day, while scrolling through Facebook, I saw a post from an old coworker. She was looking for someone to adopt her orange kitten. The moment I saw the picture, I immediately fell in love. The cat looked so much like Gingerbread because of her beautiful orange fur.

I tried to just ask it at first without a real plan of adopting, but after a few exchanged messages, my coworker decided to let me adopt the cat for free. She told me she feels like I'd be the best PAWrent. 

There was only one problem. ***The cat was a girl.***

I never wanted a female cat because Tofi was already there, and I knew what could happen if I failed to get them fixed. I told myself I would have her spayed immediately. Easy problem, right?

***Except it never happened.***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWsTTpr1jBs8EKxe7dZ6Bs1xQKdfKpnttvMFkSsbGFjge/img_5725.png)
My orange princess was too cute, too sweet, and too beautiful. I named her Tangerine, although I playfully called her ***Pongkan*** most of the time which suits her more because of her playful antics. She quickly became part of our little home.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPF8z3wrCe2mn4rY55qhi55HjWdbpZsSEhdEXcRstPkeB/img_5728.jpg)
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmf49ZV8gA7KGC84e5JH5YCbRbM2Ykc4oLY9LAthaN5be6/img_5727.jpg)
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYcigizBYCRkAgFiDJdt7kVQjJDGB24dmwgg8qmqrHKz9/img_5729.jpg)
***Tofi and Pongkan being together most of the time. I thought they looked so good as siblings. These are how our quiet days together went most of the time as a family of three.***

Then came the day *everything changed*.

At around eleven months old, Pongkan started going into heat. Suddenly, my peaceful home became a concert hall of dramatic meowing. She flirted with Tofi every single day in front of me, while he tried his best to act innocent and uninterested.

But apparently, even fluffy Persian gentlemen have limits. After days of Pongkan’s nonstop flirting, Tofi finally gave in. And just like that, Pongkan became pregnant.

That was the moment I realized I was about to become a single grandmother.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSXJincTc2pTT2KoAwPegvAqmCVL1NSXbjKKqvZFHTiVN/img_5721.jpg)
**Exactly ninety-one days later, Pongkan gave birth to three beautiful little kittens.**

At first, I was shocked and stressed because this was never part of my plan. I even thought about giving the kittens up for adoption once they got older.

But everything changed when I saw Pongkan taking care of her babies.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXjp9nd9ZSyfPzRYzKc53CnbVwhwXaHuJJbrzcs91CgXW/img_5722.jpg)
**Even though she was still a baby herself, she became such a loving mother, she loved her kittens with all her tiny orange heart. She protected them and stayed close to them every day. It touched my heart to see how much she loved them.**

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYqxG7oDHigmDcwqzEjiPimzkveuuBk4bwz6wzHLsEJgm/img_5724.jpg)
As the kittens grew bigger, they became cuter and impossible not to love. Tiny paws, tiny meows, tiny fluffy faces running around the house like little troublemakers.

Little by little, I changed my mind about giving them away. In the end, I decided to keep them.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQuS46ETMngSLmGVmQvuY9sKJLKCwRGKnEdjRpTpSwEK3/img_2916.jpg)
***Who can ever resist this cuteness? Look at him being sleepy, drunk of his mother's milk lol.***

Now, my once quiet home is full of cats, fur, meows, and lots of love. My cats created their own little family without my permission, but somehow, I ended up loving every moment of it.

I started as a single lady with one cat. **Now I am a proud and happy grandmeowmy with a big cat family.**

body.title: 🚚 Cuando la recluta recorría las calles 🇻🇪 [Esp - Eng] 🚚 When the Draft Patrol Roamed the Streets 🇻🇪
body.body:
>

***18 de mayo de 2026, Freewriters Community Daily Writing Prompt Día 3107: No voy a ser voluntario.***

Cuando leí el tema de hoy, no pude evitar soltar una sonrisa. Automáticamente mi mente viajó a mis 18 años, a esa época en Venezuela en la que uno andaba más pendiente de la famosa camioneta de la recluta que de cualquier otra cosa. 

Los que vivieron esos años seguramente me van a entender. Uno iba caminando tranquilo por la calle y, de repente, veía a lo lejos aquella camioneta llena de guardias nacionales y policías. En ese momento no hacía falta pensarlo mucho: lo primero que se activaba era el instinto de supervivencia y salíamos caminando rapidito… o corriendo, si era necesario. 

Y no es que uno no quisiera servir a la patria. Lo que pasaba era que, a esa edad, muchos soñábamos con construir nuestro propio camino y sentíamos que ese no era el destino que queríamos para nosotros. Así que cuando leí este prompt, no pude evitar recordar aquellos días con una mezcla de risa, nostalgia y la certeza de que, al final, la vida siempre termina llevándonos exactamente al lugar donde debemos estar.
__________

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbSCE1BVY3Cx2kySvR4kRQG3Xk6sdNQNDDFm4dkdBB9zP/image.png)</center>


<center>*\

*</center>

_________

Recuerdo que en aquella época la famosa recluta era un tema obligado entre los muchachos de mi generación. Apenas uno cumplía los 18 años, ya comenzaban las bromas, los consejos y, por supuesto, las estrategias para evitar caer en manos de aquella camioneta que recorría las calles buscando jóvenes para llevarlos al servicio militar. Bastaba con escuchar que alguien gritara ***“¡ahí viene la recluta!”*** para que más de uno desapareciera en cuestión de segundos. Algunos se metían en una tienda, otros cruzaban la calle y los más veloces parecían atletas olímpicos. Viéndolo hoy, la verdad es que resulta imposible no sonreír al recordarlo.

En mi caso, yo tenía muy claro que no quería ser voluntario. No porque no respetara a quienes decidían servir a la patria, sino porque sentía que mi camino iba por otro lado. En aquellos años existía la idea de que muchos de los que terminaban en la recluta eran jóvenes que todavía no tenían muy claro qué hacer con sus vidas, y yo, aunque apenas estaba comenzando, tenía el deseo de construir mi propio destino. Quería trabajar, crecer y abrirme paso por mis propios medios. Por eso cada vez que veía aquella camioneta, mi decisión estaba más firme que nunca: ese no era el camino que quería tomar.

Lo curioso es que, con el paso del tiempo, la vida terminó llevándome de todas formas a una carrera de servicio. Años más tarde ingresé a una institución policial en Venezuela, donde trabajé durante dieciocho años. Allí entendí que servir a tu país no depende de un uniforme específico, sino del compromiso con el que asumes tu trabajo y de la manera en que decides ayudar a los demás. Desde mi lugar tuve la oportunidad de acompañar a muchas personas en momentos difíciles y de aportar, a mi manera, un granito de arena a la sociedad.

Hoy miro hacia atrás y me causa gracia recordar todas aquellas carreras para escapar de la recluta. Pero también me doy cuenta de que, aun cuando en ese momento dije “no voy a ser voluntario”, la vida terminó mostrándome que sí estaba dispuesto a comprometerme con algo mucho más grande. Porque al final, todos terminamos siendo voluntarios de aquello que sentimos en el corazón. Y cuando uno encuentra su verdadero propósito, deja de correr y comienza a caminar con firmeza hacia el lugar donde realmente quiere estar.

<center>![SeparadorHive.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mballesteros/23t7YWoN53XUARh93PVvS9mqaVjjjMGSNi6uJUMjKptGwBVoiTyadsRVjRPAE27xgxsc7.png)</center>

Con el paso de los años entendí que muchas de las decisiones que tomamos de jóvenes, incluso aquellas que en su momento parecían simples ocurrencias, terminan marcando el rumbo de nuestra vida. En aquel entonces yo decía con total convicción: “No voy a ser voluntario”, sin imaginar que el tiempo me llevaría, de una u otra forma, a dedicar gran parte de mi vida al servicio de los demás.

Hoy agradezco cada experiencia vivida y cada desafío que me ayudó a convertirme en la persona que soy. Porque al final, todos terminamos comprometiéndonos con algo: con nuestra familia, con nuestros sueños, con nuestros valores y con ese deseo de dejar una huella positiva en el mundo.

Quiero agradecer a la comunidad #freewriters, en especial a @daily.prompt, @mariannewest y @felt.buzz, por este hermoso espacio donde podemos convertir recuerdos y experiencias en reflexiones que conectan con tantas personas.

Gracias por leer y acompañarme una vez más. Y ahora te pregunto, ***¿qué decisión de tu juventud marcó tu vida?*** Los leo en la caja de comentarios.

body.title: Almost There | My Introduction Story
body.body: /> “Sometimes, the dreams we end up pursuing are different from the dreams we once imagined for ourselves.” Hello Hive! 🐝 My name is Rebecca V. Gonzales, a 3rd year college student currently taking up Bachelor of Elementary Education. Honestly, if someone asked me years ago what profession I wanted, my answer would immediately be: “I want to become a flight attendant.” I dreamed of traveling around the world, meeting different people, wearing that elegant uniform, and experiencing life beyond my comfort zone. It was the profession I truly saw myself pursuing before. But as I slowly grew older, life taught me that not everything goes according to our original plans. Sometimes, we choose based on reality. Sometimes, we choose based on sacrifices. And sometimes, we choose because we want to help lessen the burden of the people we love. Taking Tourism would be expensive for our family, and deep inside, I knew it would be difficult financially. So instead of continuing that dream, I decided to pursue Education — a course that was once only my second option. At first, I honestly questioned myself a lot. “Can I really become a teacher?” “Am I capable enough?” “What if this path is not really for me?” But one person kept believing in me even during the moments I doubted myself the most — my lola.

/> I grew up with my lola, and she became one of the biggest influences in my life. She always told me that even if teachers are not always highly paid, teaching is still one of the most meaningful professions because teachers help shape the future of children. She said she could picture me standing in front of students someday — teaching with patience, kindness, and understanding. And little by little, because of her faith in me, I slowly started believing in myself too.

/>Aside from my lola, I am also deeply grateful for my siblings, especially my sister who became one of the strongest pillars of our family. She became our provider and sacrificed so much just to support me and my siblings in our studies and daily needs. Despite all the responsibilities she carries, she still manages to love us selflessly. As her younger sister, I feel so lucky because until now she still treats me like her baby sister. She loves giving me lambing, comforting me, checking on me, and making me feel loved in the simplest ways possible. Those small moments may seem ordinary to others, but for me, they became one of my biggest sources of strength. Because of them, I became more motivated to continue pursuing my studies and dreams. Someday, I want to give back to the people who sacrificed so much for me. I should already be graduating this year, but life had different plans for me. I transferred from a private college to a public university, and because of that, I had to go back to first year and retake several required subjects from my current school.

/> Honestly, it was painful at first. I felt left behind while some of my batchmates were already moving forward. There were moments when I questioned my own journey and wondered why mine had to become longer and more difficult. But eventually, I realized that life is not a race. We all have different timelines, different struggles, and different journeys. Delays do not mean failure. Sometimes, God allows detours because there are still lessons we need to learn and strengths we still need to discover within ourselves. And honestly, those extra years changed me a lot. College became one of the biggest chapters of self-discovery in my life. Little by little, I began understanding myself more. I experienced growth, maturity, disappointments, heartbreaks, silent battles, and realizations that slowly shaped me into the person I am becoming today. One of the biggest realizations I had was learning that not everyone is meant to stay in your life forever. College taught me that some friendships are only seasonal. Some people enter your life just to teach you lessons, become part of your memories, and eventually leave. I learned not to expect everyone to understand me, support me, or stay beside me forever — and honestly, accepting that reality made me emotionally stronger. It’s hard to find genuine friends who will stay with you through ups and downs, and I’m thankful that I found mine.

/>We’ve been together since first year college, through sleepless nights, stressful activities, tiring commutes, breakdowns, and happy moments. College life became lighter because of them. They are not just college friends to me. They became my safe place during some of the hardest days of my life, and I’ll always be grateful for that. 🤍 I also realized that being alone sometimes is not loneliness. Sometimes, it becomes peace. It becomes the moment where you learn how to stand on your own and focus on becoming a better version of yourself. Another thing that helped me grow was our demo teachings and classroom activities.
/>Example of Instructional materials I made.\n\n

/> At first, I was really shy whenever I had to stand in front of the class. I would overthink everything, get nervous while speaking, and become scared of making mistakes in front of other people. But through every reporting, every activity, and every demo teaching, I slowly learned how to overcome that fear. Little by little, I started building my confidence. I became more comfortable expressing myself, speaking in front of many people, and handling classroom situations during practice teaching. There are still moments when I get nervous, but compared before, I can now see how much I improved — and honestly, I feel proud of that growth. Maybe confidence is not something you instantly have. Maybe it is something you slowly build while continuously facing your fears. Outside school life, I enjoy simple things that genuinely make me happy. I love walking because it gives me peace of mind. I love singing, dancing, listening to music, and even doing house chores because simple things somehow comfort me whenever life becomes overwhelming.

/> As someone who is still figuring life out, I know I still have a long way to go. I still have fears, insecurities, and uncertainties about the future. But one thing I learned is this: Growth takes time. Healing takes time. Dreams take time. And it’s okay not to have everything figured out yet. For now, I just want to continue learning, improving myself, making my family proud, and pursuing my dreams little by little. Maybe my journey is longer than others. Maybe my dreams changed along the way. Maybe I still doubt myself sometimes. But despite everything, I am still here. Still trying. Still growing. Still believing. Maybe I’m not there yet… but I know I’m getting closer.

/>

body.title: Short temper: an uncontrollable personality? [EN/PT]
body.body: > A few days ago, I watched a video about a road rage incident. It’s so common to see this kind of thing that it almost feels like we’ve normalized explosive behavior in certain places, like traffic. But in that video, the ending was tragic, you can probably imagine what happened. The person who committed the crime, apparently full of regret, may have simply had an explosive outburst of anger in a specific moment, and maybe that’s not even their true personality. But there, in the heat of the moment, consequences were created, unfortunately for both sides. Think about it carefully: it was just a minor car collision. Just paint, plastic, and metal, abundant materials that could have been dealt with in a simple way, even if it meant some financial loss. None of that is worth more than a human life. One moment of fury, one tragedy. There are moments of fury, moments when something makes us extremely angry, and doing anything while consumed by emotion is a wrong step, because we are in an irrational state. But it’s not only about isolated moments of stress or anger, there are people who are like this all the time. This anger seems to live inside them like a flame waiting for an opportunity to burn. It’s very complicated to deal with people who naturally have this explosive personality, this emotional instability where we never know what might happen. There were only a few times when I had to deal with people with this kind of explosive personality. In those few unfortunate experiences, I noticed that, many times, the person wasn’t actually bad or malicious, they were simply that way, as if they had some kind of factory defect. If on one side there is an explosive person, naturally on the other side there are people who need to think very carefully about what they say to them, or even whether they should speak at all. It’s truly a strange feeling, it feels like there is a wild animal in the same environment, ready to devour us. There were only a few times when I had to deal with this, but I didn’t have major problems. I strongly believe that people who have this kind of temperament are aware of it. Some may even use it as an excuse for wrong attitudes. Regardless of the environment, there is a certain level of tolerance. Even if the people around them are more “good vibes,” at some point, when limits are crossed, actions need to be taken. In my opinion, you can have whatever temperament or personality you want, but what you cannot have is a lack of respect. There are limits people should never cross, whether they have a short fuse or a long fuse. I won’t judge a person for having an explosive temperament, as long as that explosion does not fall on me or on other people. You have the right to feel angry, but you do not have the right to disrespect those around you. But I also believe the person should seek medical help to treat something that could be seen as a disorder. How much can this type of behavior harm both the person who has it and the people around them? Imagine dealing with something you cannot control, hurting even the people you love. This is also a perspective we should have, because empathy includes understanding that the person causing discomfort to others is sometimes truly struggling with a difficulty. But of course, regardless of anything else, no one should accept attitudes that break the barrier of respect. But in the end, it’s not easy to deal with people who are this way. Perhaps identifying this not as a natural personality trait is the most coherent path, but rather looking at it as a psychological disorder that requires treatment. And if that is really the case, perhaps greater awareness is needed so more people seek help. But regardless of anything else, caution is necessary, because in some situations empathy needs to walk side by side with prudence. --- Credits: Translated: [Deepl](www.deepl.com/pt-BR/translator) Cover: created by [Canva.](www.canva.com) AI-generated image [ Flow]( www.labs.google/fx/pt/tools/flow) --- ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma2XinqppUM2Uvqbsii8ViPirxPmkbLmJ8FkfAbcj9EYN/image.png) Alguns dias atrás, eu vi um vídeo sobre uma briga de trânsito. É tão comum ver isso que parece até que normalizamos condutas explosivas em lugares específicos como o trânsito. Mas, nesse vídeo, o fim foi trágico, você já deve imaginar o que aconteceu. A pessoa que cometeu o crime, aparentemente muito arrependida, talvez apenas tenha tido um ato explosivo de raiva em um momento específico, e talvez essa nem seja sua personalidade. Mas ali, no calor do momento, consequências foram geradas, infelizmente para os dois lados. Pense bem: foi apenas um esbarrão de carros. Apenas tinta, plástico e ferro, materiais abundantes e que poderiam ser resolvidos de forma simples, mesmo que isso significasse algum prejuízo. Nada disso tem mais valor do que uma vida. Um momento de fúria, uma tragédia. Existem momentos de fúria, momentos em que algo nos deixa extremamente nervosos, e fazer qualquer coisa de cabeça quente é um passo errado, porque estamos em um estado irracional. Mas não somente em momentos pontuais de estresse ou raiva, existem pessoas que são assim o tempo todo. Essa raiva parece estar dentro delas como uma chama esperando uma oportunidade para queimar. É muito complicado lidar com pessoas que naturalmente possuem essa personalidade explosiva, essa instabilidade emocional em que nunca sabemos o que pode acontecer. Foram poucas as vezes em que tive de lidar com pessoas com esse tipo de personalidade explosiva. Nessas poucas e infelizes experiências, eu percebia que, muitas vezes, a pessoa não era alguém ruim ou com más intenções, ela apenas era daquele jeito, como se tivesse algum defeito de fábrica. Se de um lado existe uma pessoa explosiva, naturalmente do outro existem pessoas que precisam pensar muito bem no que falam para ela, ou até mesmo se devem falar. É realmente uma sensação estranha, parece que no mesmo ambiente existe um animal selvagem prestes a nos devorar. Foram poucas vezes que precisei lidar com isso, mas não tive grandes problemas. Eu acredito muito que as pessoas que possuem esse tipo de temperamento sabem disso. Algumas podem até usar isso como desculpa para atitudes erradas. Existe, independentemente do ambiente, uma certa tolerância. Mesmo que as pessoas ao redor sejam mais “good vibes”, em algum momento, quando limites são ultrapassados, atitudes precisam ser tomadas. Na minha opinião, você pode ter o temperamento que for, qualquer personalidade, mas o que você não pode ter é falta de respeito. Existem limites que as pessoas nunca devem ultrapassar, sejam elas de pavio curto ou pavio longo. Não vou julgar uma pessoa que tenha um temperamento explosivo, desde que essa explosão não recaia sobre mim ou sobre outras pessoas. Você tem o direito de ficar nervoso, mas não tem o direito de desrespeitar quem está por perto. Mas também acredito que a pessoa deve buscar ajuda médica para tratar algo que pode ser visto como um transtorno. O quanto esse tipo de atitude pode prejudicar quem a possui e quem está em volta? Imagine lidar com algo que não se consegue controlar, ferindo até mesmo pessoas que ama. Esse é um tipo de visão que devemos ter também, porque empatia inclui entender que quem causa esse desconforto alheio, às vezes, realmente enfrenta uma dificuldade. Mas claro, independentemente de qualquer coisa, ninguém deve aceitar atitudes que rompam a barreira do respeito. Mas, no fim, não é fácil lidar com pessoas que são dessa maneira. Talvez identificar isso não como uma personalidade natural seja o caminho mais coerente, mas sim olhar para isso como um transtorno psicológico que exige tratamento. E, se realmente for isso, talvez seja necessária uma conscientização maior para que mais pessoas busquem ajuda. Mas, independentemente de qualquer coisa, é necessário ter cuidado, porque em algumas ocasiões a empatia precisa caminhar lado a lado com a prudência. --- Credits: Translated: [Deepl](www.deepl.com/pt-BR/translator) Cover: created by [Canva.](www.canva.com) AI-generated image [ Flow]( www.labs.google/fx/pt/tools/flow) --- ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma2XinqppUM2Uvqbsii8ViPirxPmkbLmJ8FkfAbcj9EYN/image.png)

A estás alturas está demás decir que me gustan los atardeceres 🌇. Hace rato que perdí la cuenta de las publicaciones con fotos de lindos ocasos que tengo la oportunidad de fotografíar. 

Creo que haber nacido en la Barquisimeto, conocida como la ciudad crepuscular de Venezuela ha cultivado cierta sensibilidad por los ocasos. Al punto que si me preguntan ¿Cómo sería una tarde perfecta para ti? Respondería: 

*Una tarde perfecta estaría protagonizada por una buena taza de té (té negro preferiblemente) una silla cómoda, un libro y la contemplación del ocaso. Simple. Perfecto. 

Hace un par de días al ir por algunos artículos a una tienda cerca de casa pude contemplar un mágico atardecer. Me detuve a mirarlo un instante, y en ese momento tomé algunas fotos. Las mismas que ves en esta publicación. 


*Fotografía @filoriologo Redmi Note 14**Edición: Adobe Photoshop Lightroom*



***

---

##  ENGLISH VERSION

# 🌇 A magical sunset 

By now, it goes without saying that I love sunsets 🌇. I lost count long ago of how many posts I’ve shared featuring photos of the beautiful sunsets I’ve had the chance to capture. 

I think being born in Barquisimeto—known as Venezuela’s “twilight city”—has cultivated in me a certain sensitivity to sunsets. So much so that if someone asked me, “What would a perfect afternoon look like for you?” I’d answer: 

*A perfect afternoon would feature a nice cup of tea (preferably black tea), a comfortable chair, a book, and watching the sunset. Simple. Perfect. 

A couple of days ago, while I was out buying a few things at a store near my house, I got to watch a magical sunset. I stopped to look at it for a moment, and right then, I took a few photos. The same ones you see in this post.

body.title: 「Vicky's Life」短剧｜《暮雪倾城》（何聪睿x王云云）
body.body:
![IMG_0170.jpeg](https://s2.loli.net/2025/08/09/CEslBwfYnxXOTgG.jpg)

之前总听姐妹提起何聪睿的名字，我今天也终于刷到他的剧啦。不愧是比较早那批火起来的短剧男主角，这个颜值和身材真的是相当抗打，他古装现代装都很帅！

女主王云云的剧我总觉得我是看过的，长得非常耐看的女演员。两位演员的演技都比较稳，不会有太多用力过猛或是情绪不到位的情况，以后肯定会再看他俩的剧。

从剧情的角度来说，这部剧应该是打**宫斗宅斗+马甲**tags的。女主跟将军结婚当天将军出征，凯旋归来后带回一女子，不仅扣下女主嫁妆还要她答应娶女子做平妻。

这剧情我也算是看了不下十部剧了，就没见过一个出征回来跟女主安生过日子的。都说艺术源于生活高于生活，所以短剧虽然NC，但也告诉我们男人不变心母猪会上树。

从人设的角度来说，男主走的是深情那挂的，女主则是比较有能力的方式。渣男渣女的人设是比较标签化的，没有太多的心意。这部剧的人设，我觉得是比较失败的。

从拍摄手法和服化道方面，我觉得比较平庸，男主的衣服相对华丽一些，但女主主要的服装配饰都相当简单素雅——当然不排除是女主人设使然，就是觉得太简单了些。

总的来说还是不错的剧，推荐推荐。


（本篇完）


————————


喜欢影视剧、美食和旅行的天秤座80后妹纸，喜欢一切新奇温暖的事物

如果你喜欢我的文章，欢迎留言与我交流

body.title: [Eng./Esp.]   The rebellion of the hands.   ||   La rebelión de las manos.
body.body:
*** *** #
Si eres de habla hispana, la versión en español es mejor para ti; debes hacer clic 👉 [**AQUÍ**](#english)
*** ***
# ***
The rebellion of the hands
***

> Today’s quote, Monday 18 May: **“I’m not going to volunteer”**, echoes with a metallic ring through the corridors of my memory, for there was a time when my joints did not ache at dawn, when my hands were the first to answer any call to service – those days… Today, age is an inescapable physical limitation, but my retirement is also a collection of silent observations on the disillusionment I perceive in the younger generations.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeSDGApRmV9axZ86vFz5BAck2xAhWQqjFNDNe37UQtfRm/mentira.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
I hear young people repeating those words not as a gesture of apathy, but as a mantra of resistance, for they have developed an early clarity of vision. They have seen at close quarters the workings of certain NGOs and religious doctrines where the sweat of anonymity serves only to grease the wheels of the prestige of those who direct from their offices. It is the age-old tragedy of war: *the rank-and-file soldier breathes his last in the mud of the trench, the first to fall without a name or a gravestone, whilst the strategist, sheltered in the safety of the summit, observes the chaos through his binoculars, awaiting the moment to claim glory and medals. In this scenario, volunteering is sometimes perceived as a machine where the disadvantaged are the excuse and the generous are the free labour. It pains me to admit that selfless dedication has, at times, been hijacked by ego-driven marketing. ***‘I’m not going to volunteer’*** is not always a rejection of love for one’s neighbour; sometimes it is the only tangible shield left to younger generations to prevent their kindness from once again becoming the intellectual property of others who seek only to shine. *** ***

> Come and participate, there's still time. You can find all the information daily in the [#Freewritehouse](https://peakd.com/c/hive-161155/created) Community. Specifically, today's prompt post:
# **
[PROMPT: «I’m not going to volunteer»](https://peakd.com/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/18-may-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3107-im-not-going-to-volunteer)
**
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.prompt/AJmudPPCWGA6FfcXPrAmdLk2CY4mxGWYvbsFs8KPohCx9wnhBrpjcwmEyvYmxqn.jpg Cover of the initiative.
*** ***
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23swkfAXGs5WxHg49jyEWGAanWReDpMUQbxUB4FYX98iMaztGejMtj5HJUN6abwpCZhUN.png)

*** *** ### **
Dedicated to all those writers who contribute, day by day, to making our planet a better world.
** *** ***
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23vhudAgmrPvXnYXzmsiD5366jktCLxdeWqxFQg2nCeezVK4yv7CJ9dQpSevYb8nEeqTR.png) https://images.ecency.com/0x0/https://images.ecency.com/DQmbdpsZFqtrcoLk94sUV8oHkjnx8PAdgfACMfJ9UpcriNF/perfil2026_hecho_con_clipchamp_2_.gif
*** *** ***
>\n\nLa frase del día de hoy lunes 18 de mayo: **\

**,  resuena con una vibración metálica en los pasillos de mi memoria, pues, hubo un tiempo cuando mis articulaciones no protestaban al amanecer, en que mis manos eran las primeras ante cualquier llamado de servicio -aquellos días...-. Hoy, la edad es un límite físico ineludible, pero mi retiro es también un cúmulo de observaciones silenciosas sobre el desencanto que percibo en las nuevas generaciones.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWAJAa75EhL84otft8XjVu4LTWmEkDsQjrpA5rm7ajs8m/1779106004.png)
<sup>[](https://gemini.google.com/app)</sup>
</center>

Escucho a los jóvenes repetir esas palabras no como un gesto de desidia, sino como un mantra de resistencia, ya que ellos han desarrollado una lucidez temprana. Han visto de cerca los engranajes de ciertas ONG y doctrinas religiosas donde el sudor del anonimato solo sirve para aceitar el prestigio de quienes dirigen desde el despacho. Es la milenaria tragedia de la guerra: *el soldado raso entrega su aliento en el barro de la trinchera, siendo el primero en caer sin nombre ni lápida, mientras el estratega, resguardado en la seguridad de la cima, observa el caos por sus binoculares aguardando el momento de reclamar la gloria y las medallas.

En este escenario, el voluntariado se percibe a veces como una maquinaria donde los desfavorecidos son la excusa y los generosos la mano de obra gratuita.

Me duele aceptar que la entrega desinteresada ha sido, en ocasiones, secuestrada por el marketing del ego. ***\

*** no es siempre una negativa al amor al prójimo; a veces es el único escudo tangible que les queda a las nuevas generaciones para evitar que su bondad sea, una vez más, propiedad intelectual de otros que solo buscan brillar.
*** ***
